evidence: app/src/routes/abilities/[name].ts:1-62 — entire feature lives in one route directory; deleting it removes the pages
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:339-350 — the only inbound links are this self-contained section('abilities', …) block
app/src/document.ts:22-23 — nav has no Abilities link, so no shared chrome to edit
app/src/routes/404.ts:1-9 — shared not-found fallback catches any stale URLs; lib/templates.ts:53-56 notFound() shared
removability.rationale: Features map one-to-one onto route directories, with links confined to the owning pages and shared chrome unaware of them; removal leaves no dead code.

evidence: app/src/lib/templates.ts:20-41 — every Pokémon card on every page renders through one pokemonCard template
app/src/lib/api.ts:74 — sprite URLs built in one helper, so one fix covers all lists
app/src/lib/templates.ts:25,32 — CardData.id doubles as sprite key and dex number, so a fix separating species-id from Pokémon-id touches all card producers
app/src/lib/data.ts:32-49 and app/src/lib/data.ts:111-140 — both card-data producers would need the new field, plus the three list-route mappings
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:51 and app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:19 — Move API type defined twice; a PokeAPI shape change for moves is fixed in two places
app/src/lib/format.ts:7-31 — humanize/dexNumber/englishName/flavor-text each defined once and reused everywhere
changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in one obvious seam (card template, sprite helper, format helpers), but the id conflation and the duplicated Move type mean a couple of realistic fixes ripple through several files.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:4-74 — all HTTP, base URL, TTL and concurrency concerns isolated in one module; no route fetches directly
app/src/lib/data.ts:32-49 — routes consume narrow domain helpers rather than raw API internals
app/src/routes/(home).client.ts:1,17 — client enhancement is a sibling script sharing home-url.ts with the server; no server code leaks into the client bundle
app/src/lib/build.ts:7 — isBuildRender hard-codes the framework's internal 'gracile-static' build-render hostname; all 5 handlers depend on it (e.g. app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:57)

app/src/routes/(home).ts:89 vs app/src/routes/(home).client.ts:70-71 — DOM id 'results' is a string contract duplicated between server template and client script (same for 'moves-tables' at app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:276 vs [name].client.ts:67-68)
coupling.rationale: Layering is clean and server/client are well separated, but the build-guard magic hostname and the by-string DOM id contracts are tangles a maintainer can trip over.

evidence: app/src/lib/templates.ts:6-12 — CardData's optional types/note fields let one card pipeline serve home (types), abilities (hidden note) and plain lists without boolean flags
app/src/lib/data.ts:32-49 — pokemonRefsToSpecies is generic over the ref shape and preserves source, designed exactly around the Pokémon-vs-species variation the spec calls out
app/src/lib/templates.ts:57-63 — section() helper encodes the region-landmark convention once
app/src/lib/home-url.ts:1-12 — one URL builder shared by the server handler and client script
app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:19-85 — a new Items page reuses the helpers but copies the ~60-line loader+template shape; resource API types stay per-route instead of in lib/
app/src/lib/data.ts:78-86 — getTypeLabels builds a name map by fetching all 19 type details, and app/src/routes/(home).ts:15 rebuilds the same map locally instead of reusing it
abstraction_design.rationale: The shared abstractions stretch to the real variation in the app without flag creep; the gap is that per-resource loaders and API types are copied rather than factored, so a sibling resource means copy-adapt.

findings.issue: The Move API type is duplicated (also app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:51) with slightly different fields, so a PokeAPI shape change or fix to move parsing must be applied twice and can drift.
findings.suggestion: Move the canonical Move (and Ability/Species/Pokemon) API types into a shared lib/types.ts or alongside the existing shared types in app/src/lib/format.ts / data.ts, and import them in both routes.

findings.issue: CardData.id serves two roles — sprite URL key (templates.ts:25, api.ts:74) and dex number (templates.ts:32) — relying on the unstated invariant that a species' default Pokémon shares its ID; the Deoxys-style sprite fix that separates them touches every card producer (data.ts:32-49, data.ts:111-140 and the three list routes).
findings.suggestion: Make the contract explicit: add an optional spriteId (or carry the sprite URL) on CardData with a documented fallback to id, so the fix stays in lib/templates.ts plus the producers that actually know the default variety.

findings.issue: isBuildRender detects Gracile's build-time render by hard-coding the internal 'gracile-static' hostname, and all five route handlers must remember to apply it (e.g. app/src/routes/(types).ts:10, moves/[name].ts:57); a new route that forgets it fetches API data at build time, and a framework update to the stub origin breaks it silently.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the pattern once — e.g. a loadOrBuildStub(load) helper in lib/build.ts that takes the request-time loader and returns empty props during build renders — so each handler states its build stub in one line and the hostname check exists in a single place.

findings.issue: The handler boilerplate (isBuildRender stub, 404 status, 'Not found' title) is repeated verbatim in four routes (moves, abilities, types, pokemon), so an Items page starts from copy-paste.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small helper, e.g. routeHandler(load) returning { data, status } and a notFoundDocument(context), to keep new resource routes to loader + template.

findings.issue: Client enhancement scripts locate server-rendered fragments by hard-coded DOM ids ('results', 'moves-tables' at [name].client.ts:67-68); renaming the id in the server template silently breaks the progressive enhancement with no compile-time or test signal.
findings.suggestion: Define the fragment ids as exported constants from a shared module and use them in both the server templates and the client scripts.

findings.issue: getTypeLabels fetches all 19 full type details just to build a name map, and app/src/routes/(home).ts:15 rebuilds an identical map inline instead of reusing it.
findings.suggestion: Have the home route reuse getTypeLabels()/typeLabel (cached anyway) or derive labels from the TypeInfo it already loads, keeping one definition of the type-name mapping.

findings.issue: The default API base URL is duplicated in the startup log string, alongside the real definition in app/src/lib/api.ts:4.
findings.suggestion: Import the resolved API_BASE_URL from a shared module (or drop the value from the log) so the default lives in one place.

summary: This is an easy codebase to change: features map one-to-one onto route directories, every Pokémon card and every API fetch flows through single seams (pokemonCard/spriteUrl in lib/templates.ts and lib/api.ts), and server/client code is cleanly split via Gracile's .client.ts siblings with a shared URL builder. The costs are small but real: a duplicated Move API type, an id field that silently conflates species and Pokémon identity, per-route copy-adapt for new resource sections, and a magic-hostname build guard every handler must remember. Overall a solid, well-factored MPA that any maintainer could extend with confidence.
